scene: A fleet from Syracuse has docked heavy with dyed cloth and glasswork. Your wife has walked the stalls twice and returned with a very short, very specific list.

choices.label: Buy the list, all of it
choices.resultText: The blue himation appears at the next festival. Three other wives ask where it came from.

choices.label: The household budget is not a festival
choices.resultText: The list disappears without comment. So does the warmth at dinner, for a while.

scene: Your neighbor's new wall steals a hand's width of your courtyard. Your wife noticed before you did, and has opinions about men who measure twice.

choices.label: Take it to the magistrates
choices.resultText: The wall moves back a hand's width. The neighbor greets you coldly for a year, correctly.

choices.label: A hand's width is not worth a feud
choices.resultText: Peace holds. She remeasures the courtyard every month, aloud.

scene: Your wife's mother has arrived for a stay of unspecified length, with firm views on your household, your table, and — quietly — you.

choices.label: Give her the best room and your patience
choices.resultText: Three weeks of judgment, endured. Your wife notices every swallowed reply, and counts them.

choices.label: Set a courteous end date
choices.resultText: The visit ends on schedule. Letters between mother and daughter grow longer.

scene: The festival of Artemis approaches and your wife's finest himation is six years old. She has said nothing, which is how you know it matters.

choices.label: Commission a new one, quietly
choices.resultText: She finds it folded on the chest and says nothing, which is how you know it landed.

choices.label: The old one is dignified enough
choices.resultText: She wears the old one beautifully, all evening, at a certain distance from you.

scene: The woman who nursed your wife through childhood waits at your gate, widowed and without means. Your wife's face has already decided; her mouth waits for yours.

choices.label: Take her into the household
choices.resultText: An extra mouth, an extra pair of hands, and your wife humming at the loom again.

choices.label: Settle her with a pension elsewhere
choices.resultText: Provided for, at a distance. Proper, says the city. Cold, say your wife's eyes.

scene: At your own table, a guest's compliments to your wife have crossed from courtesy into performance. She handles it flawlessly. The table watches you.

choices.label: Turn it aside with a joke
choices.resultText: Laughter resets the table. The guest reddens; your wife's foot finds yours under the couch.

choices.label: Let a cold word land
choices.resultText: The guest leaves early. The story travels, in versions.

scene: Your wife wants the back court dug for a garden — thyme, poppies, a fig against the wall. The ground is currently useful for nothing but her wanting it.

choices.label: Dig it with her yourself
choices.resultText: A week of dirt and argument about where the fig goes. The fig goes where she said.

choices.label: Hire it done properly
choices.resultText: Done in two days, done well. She waters it alone at dusk.

scene: Her family's letter asks how the marriage fares. She leaves it on your table, unanswered — the reply, you understand, is to be joint.

choices.label: Write the truth together, plain
choices.resultText: An honest letter, hers and yours. Her father reads it twice, they say.

choices.label: Gild it — families want good news
choices.resultText: A beautiful letter. She signs beneath your flourishes without reading them again.

scene: The autumn storm finds the roof's weakness above the loom room. Your wife stands in the drip with a lamp, translating water into a list of repairs.

choices.label: Fix it now, storm or no
choices.resultText: Two soaked hours on a ladder. The loom stays dry and the story improves with telling.

choices.label: Patch it and wait for spring
choices.resultText: The patch holds, mostly. The loom moves rooms; the list remains.

scene: The cook and the steward have feuded into open war over a missing jar of honey. Your wife has already investigated and hands you the verdict to announce.

choices.label: Deliver her judgment as yours
choices.resultText: Peace by lunchtime. The household suspects, correctly, who actually rules it.

choices.label: Conduct your own inquiry
choices.resultText: Two more days of sulking servants to reach the same verdict. She says nothing so loudly.

scene: Your wife lays a small purse on the table — bride-coins, festival gifts, years of quiet saving — and pushes it toward your next venture without a speech.

choices.label: Accept it as the partnership it is
choices.resultText: Her coins ride with yours. Every return is counted twice now, once by each of you.

choices.label: A husband does not take his wife's purse
choices.resultText: The purse returns to its chest. Something offered once is rarely offered twice.

scene: The women of the quarter have asked your wife to lead the Thesmophoria rites this year — an honor, three days away from the household, and no men's business at all.

choices.label: Send her with pride and provisions
choices.resultText: She returns three days later, taller somehow. The other wives greet her first now.

choices.label: The household cannot spare her
choices.resultText: Another wife leads the rites. Yours keeps the house perfectly, silently.

scene: You wake shouting from a dream of drowning, again. Your wife is already awake, lamp lit, as though she has been keeping watch for some time.

choices.label: Tell her the dream, all of it
choices.resultText: Spoken aloud, the sea shrinks. She keeps the lamp burning anyway.

choices.label: It is nothing — sleep
choices.resultText: She sleeps, or pretends to. The lamp stays within reach of her hand.

scene: A dry summer. Your cistern holds; the neighbors' don't. Your wife has been giving water at the gate in cups, and the cups are becoming buckets.

choices.label: Open the cistern to the street
choices.resultText: Your gate becomes the quarter's well. The debt the street owes you has no number, which is the best kind.

choices.label: Guard it — charity ends where thirst begins
choices.resultText: The cistern lasts the summer. So does the memory of the latch.

scene: Another house's wife is selling cloth in your wife's border pattern — the one her grandmother carried from Phocaea. Your wife is calm in the way of banked fires.

choices.label: Raise it with the other husband
choices.resultText: The pattern vanishes from their stall. The two wives exchange festival courtesies like duelists.

choices.label: Let the work speak — hers is better
choices.resultText: Hers is better, and the buyers know it. She weaves a new border anyway, unshared.

scene: A widow of the last border skirmish stands at your gate with two children and her husband's shield to sell. Your wife has already fed the children.

choices.label: Buy the shield at a soldier's price
choices.resultText: The shield hangs in your hall, unsold in every way that matters. The widow's boys run your errands now.

choices.label: Direct her to the temple's charity
choices.resultText: The temple does its duty. Your wife adds a coin to the widow's hand at the gate, from her own purse, visibly.

scene: The anniversary of her father's death. She has prepared the offerings alone and asks only whether you will stand with her at the tomb.

choices.label: Stand with her, the full rites
choices.resultText: Wine on old stone, his name said aloud. Walking home she holds your arm with both hands.

choices.label: Attend briefly — the day is full
choices.resultText: You arrive for the last libation. She notices exactly when you arrived.

scene: The coldest morning of the year. The brazier glows, the shutters are sealed, and your wife observes that no business in Massalia is worth this particular dawn.

choices.label: She is entirely correct
choices.resultText: A day of warmth, wine, and talk that goes nowhere on purpose. The city survives without you.

choices.label: Wrap up — the city does not pause
choices.resultText: Profitable, frozen hours. You return to a warmth that has moved to her side of it.

scene: A helpful acquaintance mentions you were seen leaving a certain house on the hill. You were there on business. Your wife has heard the version without the business.

choices.label: Tell her the whole of it, unasked
choices.resultText: The account balances. She believes you — and mentions, lightly, that she always hears everything.

choices.label: Dignify nothing — rumors starve
choices.resultText: The rumor starves slowly. Dinner is punctual and precise for a month.

scene: Combing her hair at the window, your wife finds her first grey strand, holds it to the light, and asks you — dangerously — whether you noticed it before she did.

choices.label: Say it suits her, and mean it
choices.resultText: The strand stays. So does the way she looked at you when you said it.

choices.label: Make a joke about matching yours
choices.resultText: Laughter, and a comb thrown with fair accuracy. An honorable draw.

scene: Your wife has taken a vow — nine days of fasting for the household's fortune. She grows pale by the fifth day and will not hear of stopping.

choices.label: Share the fast's final days with her
choices.resultText: Hunger, prayer, and a strange lightness. The vow completes; the household eats like kings after.

choices.label: Bring the physician to overrule the vow
choices.resultText: The physician wins. The vow is broken gently, and grieved quietly for a season.

scene: A trader from Cyprus has perfumed oils that cost what a mule costs. Your wife has already tried three and reserved two, pending — technically — your approval.

choices.label: Approve the reservation
choices.resultText: The house smells of Cyprus for a month. So, faintly, do all your correspondence and half your friends.

choices.label: One jar. Marriage is compromise
choices.resultText: One jar, made to last, deployed strategically. The trader bows to her at the next docking.

scene: A letter meant for your rival was delivered to your house by a confused courier. It is sealed. Your wife has held it to the lamp and learned things anyway.

choices.label: Open it — the gods sent it here
choices.resultText: The seal is restored expertly — she has done this before, you note. What you learned pays for the guilt.

choices.label: Send it on untouched
choices.resultText: The courier departs with the letter and your reputation intact. She recites its likely contents from the lamp-shadows anyway, and is probably right.

scene: Your wife has begun hosting the wives of powerful men for weaving afternoons. The weaving is real. So is the intelligence that comes home with the wool.

choices.label: Fund the afternoons generously
choices.resultText: You learn which magistrate cannot pay his debts and which captain is selling his ship, weeks early.

choices.label: Such gatherings breed talk
choices.resultText: The afternoons end. The wives gather elsewhere now, and the wool comes home silent.

scene: At last night's feast your wife swore — loudly, publicly — that your house would fund the spring regatta's prize. You learned of your generosity this morning.

choices.label: Honor her oath in full
choices.resultText: The prize bears your house's name. She toasts you at the regatta as though it were your idea, which by then everyone believes.

choices.label: Renegotiate it down to a wreath
choices.resultText: A wreath is offered. The word 'wreath' is pronounced around the harbor with great enjoyment for a season.

scene: Her father has died. The inheritance is real — but her brothers' letter observes that a share flowing to your house should flow back in loyalty at the next election.

choices.label: Accept the share and the leash
choices.resultText: The silver arrives. So, at intervals, do the brothers' expectations, itemized.

choices.label: Waive the share — grief owes nothing
choices.resultText: Her brothers are stunned into respect. She grieves freely, unbought, and does not forget which you chose.

scene: You practice tomorrow's council speech at dinner. Your wife listens with her scroll-trained ear, then rewrites your ending on the back of a household tablet.

choices.label: Deliver her ending
choices.resultText: The ending lands like a thrown spear. Two councilors ask who taught you rhetoric. You change the subject.

choices.label: A man speaks his own words
choices.resultText: Your ending is adequate. She mouths hers, silently, from memory, at breakfast.

scene: Your wife has pledged a tenth of the season's household surplus to the temple of Artemis — before mentioning the arithmetic to you.

choices.label: Pay the tithe gladly
choices.resultText: The priestesses name your house in the blessing. She walks to temple with her chin high all season.

choices.label: A twentieth honors the goddess equally
choices.resultText: The goddess, presumably, forgives. Your wife's account is longer-running.

scene: Your wife has posted the household's duties on the wall — by name, by hour, in her square handwriting. The servants call it, out of her hearing, the phalanx.

choices.label: Back the regime completely
choices.resultText: The house runs like a trireme at ramming speed. Guests remark on it. She almost smiles.

choices.label: Soften it — a home is not a barracks
choices.resultText: The wall list acquires exceptions. So does everything else, gradually.

scene: Your wife has renegotiated the household's oil, grain, and wool contracts without telling you, and presents the savings like a hunting trophy.

choices.label: Praise the hunt and bank it
choices.resultText: The savings are real. The merchants of three stalls now flinch pleasantly when she approaches.

choices.label: Smooth the feathers she ruffled
choices.resultText: You overpay one merchant to keep the peace. She recalculates the loss aloud, monthly.

scene: At the festival seating, your wife was placed below a newer house's bride. She sat, smiled through it magnificently, and has now raised the matter once, at home, in a voice of marble.

choices.label: Raise it with the festival archons
choices.resultText: Next festival, the seating corrects itself. Nothing was said. Everything was understood.

choices.label: Seats are wood — dignity is carried
choices.resultText: She agrees completely, in the tone that means the opposite, and carries her dignity to the lower bench all season.

scene: Halfway through the feast you are hosting, your wife has vanished. You find her on the dark stair with the wine she rescued, breathing like a diver surfaced.

choices.label: Cover her absence and join her
choices.resultText: Ten stolen minutes on a cold stair, the feast roaring beyond the door. The best part of the evening, you both agree.

choices.label: The hostess must return
choices.resultText: She returns and performs flawlessly. The performance costs what performances cost; she pays it alone.

scene: You cannot remember the last evening your courtyard held fewer than nine guests. Your wife collects people the way other wives collect combs. Tonight you wanted quiet.

choices.label: Surrender — the house is a harbor
choices.resultText: Eleven guests, two lyres, one poet. You know everything happening in Massalia by midnight.

choices.label: Claim one evening for two
choices.resultText: The gate stays barred. She spends the evening happily telling you about all the people who aren't there.

scene: Your wife has begun watering your wine a shade further each week, so gradually you only noticed today. She meets your look with the expression of a woman who counts your mornings-after.

choices.label: Accept the watering with grace
choices.resultText: Clearer mornings, longer evenings. You concede — internally, never aloud — that she was right.

choices.label: A man pours his own measure
choices.resultText: You pour unwatered. She sets a second jug of plain water beside it, silently refilled, forever.

scene: A guest at your table asks your wife, carelessly, what she thinks of his new venture. She tells him. Precisely. The venture is his life's savings.

choices.label: Stand behind every word
choices.resultText: He leaves wounded and returns a month later, venture restructured, to thank her. Slowly, her verdicts become sought.

choices.label: Soften it into diplomacy after
choices.resultText: Your smoothing-over undoes half her warning. He proceeds. The venture proceeds accordingly.

scene: Fire in the tenement two doors down. You arrive to find your wife already in the bucket line, hem tied up, directing the water like a taxiarch.

choices.label: Take the bucket beside her
choices.resultText: The fire dies at the second floor. You are both grey with ash and briefly famous in the quarter.

choices.label: Pull her back — it is not your fire
choices.resultText: She comes, at the third asking. The fire is beaten without you both. The quarter remembers who was in the line.

scene: Your youngest's first clear word arrives at dinner — and it is Gaulish, learned from the nurse. The household freezes mid-bite, waiting for your face.

choices.label: Laugh and answer in Gaulish
choices.resultText: The table exhales into laughter. The child now has two words for bread and uses both, loudly.

choices.label: Gently insist the nurse speak Greek
choices.resultText: Greek prevails at the hearth. The Gaulish word survives underground, as banned words do.

scene: The youngest is cutting teeth and the whole house knows it, hourly. The nurse suggests a Gaulish remedy of rubbed herbs; the physician suggests patience at a fee.

choices.label: Try the nurse's remedy
choices.resultText: Whatever the herb is, it works by midnight. The physician pronounces it coincidence, at no charge for the opinion.

choices.label: Buy the physician's patience
choices.resultText: Patience is prescribed and eventually delivered. The tooth arrives on its own schedule, as teeth do.

scene: A shriek from the hall: the youngest, newly crawling, was found a hand's reach from the open hearth. The nurse is weeping; your wife's face asks what happens next.

choices.label: Comfort the nurse — children are quick
choices.resultText: The nurse steadies. A fender of woven withies appears around the hearth by evening, her own making.

choices.label: Replace the nurse — once is enough
choices.resultText: A new nurse, careful and a stranger. The child cries for the old one for a week.

scene: A vase-painter down on his luck offers to paint the youngest into a small votive scene — cheap immortality, he says, for a child who will never again be this small.

choices.label: Commission the votive
choices.resultText: A tiny figure among the olive branches, unmistakably yours. It outlasts everyone who ever explains it.

choices.label: Coin is not for keepsakes
choices.resultText: The painter moves on. The smallness moves on too, unrecorded, as he said it would.

scene: Your son's new slingshot and a merchant's best amphora have concluded their brief acquaintance. The merchant stands at your gate holding the pieces and an invoice.

choices.label: Pay, then teach him aim properly
choices.resultText: The debt is settled and the lessons begin. By autumn he can hit a fig at thirty paces, and knows what figs cost.

choices.label: The boy works off the debt himself
choices.resultText: A month of sweeping the merchant's stall. He returns knowing the price of amphorae and the smell of honest work.

scene: Your daughter has smuggled a harbor stray into the storeroom and provisioned it better than some garrisons. It has three legs, no manners, and her whole heart.

choices.label: The house has room for a bad dog
choices.resultText: The dog adopts the household in return. It guards the gate ferociously against pelicans and no one else.

choices.label: It belongs to the harbor, gently
choices.resultText: The dog is returned to its wharf. Your daughter provisions it there instead, daily, on principle.

scene: An itinerant grammarian offers lessons — letters, numbers, a little Homer — for a child of the house. His robe is threadbare; his Greek is Athenian and beautiful.

choices.label: Hire him for a season
choices.resultText: By summer the child reads the shop-signs aloud on every walk, insufferably. Worth every obol.

choices.label: Lessons can wait a year
choices.resultText: The grammarian teaches a rival's children instead. Their shop-sign reading is equally insufferable and one year ahead.

scene: A child of yours followed a festival procession and vanished into the agora for three hours, returned at last by an Etruscan trader who refused a reward with great ceremony.

choices.label: Host the trader as a guest-friend
choices.resultText: A dinner becomes a friendship becomes, years later, a trading contact in Etruria. The child claims full credit.

choices.label: Thanks, and a firmer hand at festivals
choices.resultText: Proper gratitude, properly bounded. Festival days now feature a rope around a small wrist.

scene: The men of the quarter ride out for boar next week. Your son, fourteen and vibrating, has asked to come — not to watch. To carry a spear.

choices.label: Take him, spear and all
choices.resultText: He holds the line when the boar breaks left, white-faced and rooted. The men pour him his first field wine.

choices.label: Next year — this year he watches
choices.resultText: He watches from the wagon with murder in his eyes. Next year is invoked at every meal.

scene: The finest weaver in Massalia has seen your daughter's work at festival and offers to take her as apprentice — an honor, and three days a week away from your household.

choices.label: Send her to the master
choices.resultText: Within a year her cloth sells before it leaves the loom. The master calls her 'my best' within earshot of other mothers.

choices.label: Her mother's loom taught her this well
choices.resultText: She keeps weaving at home, brilliantly, with one window always angled toward the master's workshop.

scene: Your almost-grown child has fallen in with the dock youths — dice, dares, and a vocabulary that arrived at dinner last night like a dropped fish.

choices.label: Cut the company off cleanly
choices.resultText: The docks are forbidden. The vocabulary lingers a season; the dice come home in a confiscated cup.

choices.label: Channel it — give the pack honest work
choices.resultText: You hire the whole pack to haul for the warehouse. Half of them turn out useful. Your child is promoted to foreman of five scoundrels, glowing.

scene: At the tomb-sweeping, your eldest asks — carefully, casually — which of the children will carry the house when you are gone. The younger ones have stopped breathing to listen.

choices.label: Name the order plainly, now
choices.resultText: The order is spoken at the tomb, witnessed by ancestors. Clarity lands hard and settles well.

choices.label: The gods decide such things
choices.resultText: The question retreats, unanswered. It returns every tomb-sweeping after, better prepared.

scene: You discover your son on the courtyard bench, draped in a tablecloth, delivering your last council speech to an audience of hens — gestures, pauses, and all.

choices.label: Coach the performance properly
choices.resultText: The hens receive a masterclass. Years on, his first real speech carries your pauses, improved.

choices.label: A magistrate's speech is not theater
choices.resultText: The tablecloth is retired. The imitation continues, you are reliably informed, at a smaller venue.

scene: Your daughter has climbed to the roof again to count stars, and asks whether it is true a Massaliote once sailed to where the sun forgets to set.

choices.label: Tell her the whole of Pytheas's voyage
choices.resultText: Thule, the amber coasts, the sleepless sun — she repeats it to the household for a month, adding sea monsters where the record is thin.

choices.label: Stars keep — sleep does not
choices.resultText: She descends under protest. The next clear night, a stool is already positioned on the roof.

scene: At the Anthesteria your almost-grown child was served unwatered wine by laughing friends and came home singing a rowing song, sideways.

choices.label: Let the morning teach the lesson
choices.resultText: The morning teaches comprehensively. Water is requested, in a small voice, with breakfast.

choices.label: A stern word tonight, headache or no
choices.resultText: The lecture lands on a wincing audience. Both lessons — yours and the morning's — are retained.

scene: A child of yours and a cousin from her brother's house have fought at the family gathering — over a wooden horse, allegedly, though testimony varies. Both houses watched.

choices.label: Make them repair the horse together
choices.resultText: An hour of sullen joint carpentry becomes, by the glue stage, an alliance. The horse survives; so does the peace between houses.

choices.label: Take your child's side on principle
choices.resultText: Your child is vindicated and delighted. Her brother's house keeps a cooler distance for a season.

scene: Two clients — a shipowner and a young officer — have discovered they share a devotion to the same woman of your house, and are one insult from settling it with steel in your courtyard.

choices.label: Separate their evenings forever
choices.resultText: A quiet recalibration of invitations. They never meet again, and each believes he won.

choices.label: Let them compete — in gifts, publicly
choices.resultText: The rivalry becomes the season's entertainment and the house's best quarter. Steel stays sheathed; purses do not.

scene: A magistrate wishes to book the entire house for one night — his guests, his wine, his terms, and a sum that would carry you through winter. His terms include discretion so total it borders on ownership.

choices.label: Take the night and the terms
choices.resultText: The night passes flawlessly and invisibly. What was discussed on your couches never happened, anywhere, to anyone.

choices.label: The house has one mistress
choices.resultText: He books a rival house. What was discussed there reaches you anyway, in three days, through the wool market.

scene: The best-loved woman of your house burns with the marsh fever. The physician's price is steep; the clients' inquiries after her are steeper in their own way.

choices.label: Spare nothing for her care
choices.resultText: Three weeks of broth and vigil. She returns to the couches thinner and, by some alchemy, more requested than ever.

choices.label: Send her to the temple healers
choices.resultText: Artemis's women take her in. She returns healed and quietly different, with a debt she pays the temple, not you.

scene: A citizen's wife stands at your back door at midnight, veiled, bruised, asking shelter of the only house in Massalia her husband cannot enter without scandal.

choices.label: Shelter her — the house protects women
choices.resultText: Three days behind your walls while her brothers are summoned. The husband rages at your gate and dares not pass it. Half the city's wives owe you now.

choices.label: The house cannot afford this war
choices.resultText: You send her to the temple with an escort and a purse. Safer for the house. The door closes on her thanks, which you do not hear.

scene: A young poet, briefly wealthy in love and permanently poor in coin, has written a cycle of verses naming your house — its lamps, its laughter, one woman's particular way of turning her head.

choices.label: Become his patron before someone else does
choices.resultText: The verses spread from symposium to symposium with your house as their heaven. Bookings follow the poetry.

choices.label: Buy the verses and burn them
choices.resultText: The cycle vanishes; discretion is preserved. One stanza escapes anyway and is sung at weddings for a generation, author unknown.

scene: The lender who financed your house's second floor has died, and his heir — a sharp-eyed nephew — calls the whole debt within the month, hoping to squeeze the house into his hands.

choices.label: Pay it whole, whatever it empties
choices.resultText: The debt clears and the nephew's lever breaks in his hand. The house stands unowned by anyone but you, provably.

choices.label: Counter with what you know of him
choices.resultText: The nephew recalls, upon reflection, certain evenings in your house he would prefer stayed unrecalled. New terms: the old terms.

scene: A new house has opened by the harbor — Ionian fashions, kithara players from Ephesus, prices set to bleed you. Your best clients are curious the way men are curious.

choices.label: Answer with something older — pure Massaliote craft
choices.resultText: You stage an evening of local poetry and Phocaean songs no Ionian house can fake. The curious return, comparing notes in your favor.

choices.label: Novelty starves — hold your prices
choices.resultText: By spring the Ionian house has halved its kithara players. Your ledger never noticed the war.

scene: The eldest woman of your house — she taught you the ledger, and half of everything else — asks to retire to a cottage by the shrine while her savings still buy one.

choices.label: Provision the cottage yourself, fully
choices.resultText: She retires like a strategos, honored. Every woman in the house sees exactly what loyal service purchases.

choices.label: Her savings are hers; the choice too
choices.resultText: She manages, just. The younger women recalculate their own savings that week, all of them.

scene: One of your women is with child and has hidden it past hiding. The father is a client of standing who does not know, or knows and waits to see what you do.

choices.label: Fold her into the household's care
choices.resultText: She keeps her place, then her child, within your walls. The house gains a baby, a secret held in common, and a loyalty no coin buys.

choices.label: Negotiate quietly with the father
choices.resultText: A settlement, discreet and sufficient. The client pays his invisible account for years without complaint, which is its own confession.

scene: A priestess of Artemis proposes something unheard of: your women to sing at the goddess's night rite — the sacred and the profane sharing one torchlight, scandalizing everyone correctly.

choices.label: Accept — the goddess loves all her women
choices.resultText: The night rite is the year's wonder. For one torchlit hour, no one in Massalia can say what your house is, only that it sang.

choices.label: Keep the lamps and altars separate
choices.resultText: The rite proceeds without you, conventionally. The priestess sends wine anyway, with a note: 'Next year.'

scene: A dockside informer offers to sell you what your clients say about your house in other houses — and, unspoken, to sell what he learns in yours the same way.

choices.label: Buy once, learn his network, then bar him
choices.resultText: His list is instructive twice over: what is said, and who talks. The door closes on him knowing you know.

choices.label: Bar him at the first sentence
choices.resultText: Word travels that your house does not trade in its guests. Men speak more freely on your couches, which was always the better merchandise.

scene: A wealthy widower — kind, unhandsome, sincere — offers you marriage, retirement, respectability: everything the trade cannot give, priced at everything you have built.

choices.label: Entertain the dream for one evening
choices.resultText: One evening of imagining another life, honestly. In the morning you open the ledger with something like renewed vows.

choices.label: Refuse him kindly, and completely
choices.resultText: He takes it as gracefully as he offered. He remains a friend of the house for life — its most loyal, least demanding one.
